name: Brahmā
summary: Lineage contribution (Āyurveda): the first knower of the Veda of life, who 'remembering' it taught it to Prajāpati (AHS Sū 1.3; Ca Sū 1.4; Su Sū 1.20); in the Suśruta he first made it in a hundred thousand verses and a thousand chapters, then divided it eightfold for short-lived men (Su Sū 1.6).

name: Dakṣa Prajāpati
summary: The Prajāpati who received Āyurveda from Brahmā and taught it to the Aśvins (Ca Sū 1.4; Su Sū 1.20; AHS Sū 1.3); the Bhāvaprakāśa names him Dakṣa.
notes: Caraka, Suśruta and Vāgbhaṭa say only 'Prajāpati'; Bhāvaprakāśa Pūrva 1.6 and the commentators say Dakṣa.

name: The Aśvins
summary: The twin physicians of the gods (Nāsatyas, Dasras), who learnt Āyurveda from Prajāpati and taught it to Indra; they rejoined the head of the sacrifice cut off by Rudra, restored Pūṣan's teeth, Bhaga's eyes and Indra's arm, cured the Moon of consumption and made the aged Cyavana young (Su Sū 1.17; Ca Ci 1.4.41-44; Bhāvaprakāśa Pūrva 1.8-13).

name: Indra (Śakra)
summary: Lineage contribution (Āyurveda): received Āyurveda from the Aśvins and taught it — to Bharadvāja, who came on behalf of the sages (Ca Sū 1.3-26); to Dhanvantari (Su Sū 1.20); to Ātreya and the other sages (AHS Sū 1.3; Bhāvaprakāśa); and he revealed the rejuvenating herbs of the Himalaya to the sages (Ca Ci 1.4.3-6).

name: Bharadvāja
summary: Lineage contribution (Āyurveda): the sage who, chosen by the assembly of sages in the Himalaya when disease obstructed austerity and study, went to Indra 'seeking long life', learnt the threefold Āyurveda (cause, sign, remedy), gained immeasurable life and taught it to the sages (Ca Sū 1.3-27).
notes: Distinct in this unit from Kumāraśiras Bharadvāja who speaks in Ca Sū 12, 26 and Śā 6 (tch:kumarasiras-bharadvaja); the objector of Ca Śā 3.4 is simply 'Bharadvāja'.

name: Punarvasu Ātreya
summary: The teacher of the Caraka Saṃhitā: out of friendliness and compassion for all beings he taught Āyurveda to six disciples — Agniveśa, Bhela, Jatūkarṇa, Parāśara, Hārīta and Kṣārapāṇi (Ca Sū 1.30-31) — and in every chapter 'thus spoke the venerable Ātreya'. He presides over the debates of the sages and closes them (Sū 12.13, 25.26-29, 26.9).
places: Kāmpilya in Pañcāla, by the Gaṅgā (Ca Vi 3.3)
notes: Caraka has Ātreya learn from Bharadvāja (implied by Sū 1.26-30); the Bhāvaprakāśa has Ātreya go to Indra himself. Bhikṣu Ātreya of Ca Sū 25.24 is a different speaker. Whether Kṛṣṇātreya (a śālākya authority in later sources) is the same person is disputed.

name: Agniveśa
summary: The first of Ātreya's disciples to compose a tantra (Ca Sū 1.32); he is the questioner throughout the Caraka Saṃhitā, whose text is 'the tantra made by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka' (colophons).

name: Bhela
summary: Disciple of Ātreya whose tantra was read out to the assembly (Ca Sū 1.31-33); the partly surviving Bhela Saṃhitā bears his name.

name: Jatūkarṇa
summary: One of Ātreya's six disciples, each of whom composed his own tantra and read it to Ātreya and the sages (Ca Sū 1.31-33).
notes: Whether this is the same person as the homonymous sage of other traditions is not settled; kept separate.

name: Parāśara (disciple of Ātreya)
summary: One of Ātreya's six disciples, each of whom composed his own tantra and read it to Ātreya and the sages (Ca Sū 1.31-33).
notes: Whether this is the same person as the homonymous sage of other traditions is not settled; kept separate.

name: Hārīta (disciple of Ātreya)
summary: One of Ātreya's six disciples, each of whom composed his own tantra and read it to Ātreya and the sages (Ca Sū 1.31-33).
notes: Whether this is the same person as the homonymous sage of other traditions is not settled; kept separate.

name: Kṣārapāṇi
summary: One of Ātreya's six disciples, each of whom composed his own tantra and read it to Ātreya and the sages (Ca Sū 1.31-33).
notes: Whether this is the same person as the homonymous sage of other traditions is not settled; kept separate.

name: Caraka
summary: The redactor (pratisaṃskartā) of Agniveśa's tantra: 'the redactor expands what is said briefly and condenses what is too long, and makes an old tantra new' (Ca Si 12.36-37). In the Bhāvaprakāśa he is a portion of the thousand-headed Śeṣa who came to earth 'like a spy' (cara) and was born as a sage's son; Cakrapāṇi salutes the lord of serpents who removed the faults of mind, speech and body by the Pātañjala, the Mahābhāṣya and Caraka's redaction.
notes: A Buddhist narrative preserved in Chinese makes a physician Caraka attend King Kaniṣka; scholars differ on whether this is the redactor (scholarly hypothesis, recalled).

name: Dṛḍhabala
summary: Born in the city of Pañcanada, he completed Caraka's redaction, a third of which was missing, by gleaning from many tantras seventeen chapters of the Cikitsā and the Kalpa and Siddhi sections (Ca Si 12.38-40).

name: Dhanvantari (Divodāsa, king of Kāśī)
summary: Lineage contribution (Āyurveda): 'I am Dhanvantari, the first god, remover of old age, disease and death for the immortals, come again to earth to teach the limb of surgery with the other limbs' (Su Sū 1.21). As King Divodāsa of Kāśī he taught Aupadhenava, Vaitaraṇa, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata, Karavīrya, Gopurarakṣita, Suśruta and others (Su Sū 1.3), having learnt Āyurveda from Indra (Su Sū 1.20); the Bhāvaprakāśa tells how Indra sent him to be born in Kāśī.
notes: Ca Śā 6.21 cites Dhanvantari's view that all limbs of the embryo form at once.

name: Suśruta
summary: The student who put the questions to Divodāsa Dhanvantari on behalf of his fellows, who asked that surgery be made the root of the teaching (Su Sū 1.10-14); the Suśruta Saṃhitā is addressed to him ('vatsa Suśruta').
notes: Later tradition makes him a son of Viśvāmitra (recalled, not checked).

name: Aupadhenava
summary: One of Suśruta's fellow students who approached Divodāsa Dhanvantari for the teaching (Su Sū 1.3).
notes: Later commentators cite tantras under some of these names (Aupadhenava, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata) — recalled, not checked.

name: Vaitaraṇa
summary: One of Suśruta's fellow students who approached Divodāsa Dhanvantari for the teaching (Su Sū 1.3).
notes: Later commentators cite tantras under some of these names (Aupadhenava, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata) — recalled, not checked.

name: Aurabhra
summary: One of Suśruta's fellow students who approached Divodāsa Dhanvantari for the teaching (Su Sū 1.3).
notes: Later commentators cite tantras under some of these names (Aupadhenava, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata) — recalled, not checked.

name: Pauṣkalāvata
summary: One of Suśruta's fellow students who approached Divodāsa Dhanvantari for the teaching (Su Sū 1.3).
notes: Later commentators cite tantras under some of these names (Aupadhenava, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata) — recalled, not checked.

name: Karavīrya
summary: One of Suśruta's fellow students who approached Divodāsa Dhanvantari for the teaching (Su Sū 1.3).
notes: Later commentators cite tantras under some of these names (Aupadhenava, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata) — recalled, not checked.

name: Gopurarakṣita
summary: One of Suśruta's fellow students who approached Divodāsa Dhanvantari for the teaching (Su Sū 1.3).
notes: Later commentators cite tantras under some of these names (Aupadhenava, Aurabhra, Pauṣkalāvata) — recalled, not checked.

name: Nāgārjuna (the siddha, alchemist and physician)
summary: Named by Ḍalhaṇa as the redactor of the Suśruta Saṃhitā; counted among the twenty-seven siddhas of rasa (Rasaratnasamuccaya 1.4) and cited in the Rasaratnākara (Rasa-khaṇḍa 1.17) as having taught for the sick; alchemical works (Rasendramaṅgala) are attributed to him.
notes: Tibetan and some Indian traditions identify him with the Madhyamaka philosopher (tch:nagarjuna); scholars usually distinguish one or more later Nāgārjunas. Kept separate here.

name: Mārīca Kaśyapa
summary: The teacher of children's medicine whose instruction to Vṛddha Jīvaka forms the Kāśyapa Saṃhitā; in Ca Śā 6.21 'Mārīci Kaśyapa' holds that the order of the embryo's limbs cannot be known, being beyond perception.

name: Vṛddha Jīvaka
summary: The disciple who received and set down Mārīca Kaśyapa's teaching on children's medicine (Kāśyapa Saṃhitā).

name: Vātsya (redactor of the Kāśyapa Saṃhitā)
summary: In the Kāśyapa Saṃhitā's own account, restored the lost tantra of Vṛddha Jīvaka.

name: Kumāraśiras Bharadvāja
summary: Speaker in the assemblies: vāyu is provoked by the repeated use of what shares its qualities (Ca Sū 12.5); there are five tastes — earthy, watery, fiery, airy and spatial (Sū 26.8); the head forms first in the embryo, as the seat of the senses (Śā 6.21).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Kāṅkāyana, the physician of Bāhlīka
summary: Speaker: the opposite of the provoking factors pacifies vāyu (Ca Sū 12.6); tastes are innumerable (Sū 26.8); the heart forms first, as the seat of consciousness (Śā 6.21); Prajāpati is the creator of the person and of disease (Sū 25.23).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Baḍiśa Dhāmārgava
summary: Speaker: how vāyu, formless and unstable, is provoked and pacified through the body's condition (Ca Sū 12.7); eight tastes (Sū 26.8); the hands and feet form first (Śā 6.21).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Vāyorvida (the royal sage)
summary: The royal sage who praised vāyu as the upholder of body and world, 'the lord Vāyu himself' (Ca Sū 12.8, 12.10); six tastes defined by qualities (Sū 26.8); in Sū 25.12-13 (as Vāryovida) he holds that beings and diseases arise from rasa (water).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Marīci (in Caraka's assembly)
summary: Speaker: fire within pitta, provoked or unprovoked, does good and ill in the body (Ca Sū 12.11).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Kāpya
summary: Speaker: Soma within kapha does good and ill in the body (Ca Sū 12.12).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Bhadrakāpya
summary: Speaker: there is one taste only, not other than water (Ca Sū 26.8); the person and disease arise from karma (Sū 25.18-19); the navel forms first (Śā 6.21).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Kuśa Sāṅkṛtyāyana
summary: Opened the debate on vāyu by naming its six qualities (Ca Sū 12.4).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Pārīkṣi Maudgalya
summary: Speaker: the person and his diseases are born of the self, the conscious principle being the cause (Ca Sū 25.8-9).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Śaraloman
summary: Speaker: the mind (sattva) pervaded by rajas and tamas is the cause of the body and of disorders (Ca Sū 25.10-11).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Hiraṇyākṣa Kauśika
summary: Speaker: the person and diseases arise from the six dhātus, as the first Sāṃkhyas taught (Ca Sū 25.14-15); four tastes (Sū 26.8).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Bhikṣu Ātreya
summary: Speaker: the person and diseases arise from time (Ca Sū 25.24-25); named in the assembly of sages (Ca Sū 1.9).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Vāmaka, king of Kāśī
summary: Put to the sages the question whether the person and his diseases arise from the same source (Ca Sū 25.5-6), and asked what makes them grow (25.30).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Maitreya (in Caraka's assembly)
summary: Objected that medicine is ineffective, since some treated patients die and some untreated recover (Ca Sū 10.4); answered by Ātreya.
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Nimi, king of Videha
summary: Speaker: seven tastes, counting alkali (Ca Sū 26.8); in later tradition the author of a lost tantra of eye and head disease.
notes: Speaker ref checked; the lost tantra is recalled only.

name: Śākunteya
summary: A brahmin speaker: two tastes, the eliminating and the pacifying (Ca Sū 26.8).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Pūrṇākṣa Maudgalya
summary: Speaker: three tastes (Ca Sū 26.8).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Bhadraśaunaka
summary: Speaker: the large intestine and anus form first, as the seat of wind (Ca Śā 6.21).
notes: Refs checked against the DCS e-text of the Caraka Saṃhitā.

name: Vāgbhaṭa
summary: Author of the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya, 'son of Siṃhagupta, lord of physicians' (colophons), who made a verse 'heart' of the eight-limbed medicine from the scattered tantras of Agniveśa and the others (AHS Sū 1.3-5). He opens with homage to the unprecedented physician who destroyed the diseases of passion, and ends by asking readers to take what is well said without partisanship.
notes: Buddhist affiliation is a scholarly inference from AHS Sū 1.1 and 2.21-22. Some later authors distinguish an elder Vāgbhaṭa (Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha). The Rasaratnasamuccaya's author also calls himself son of Siṃhagupta.

name: Mādhavakara
summary: Author of the Rugviniścaya (Mādhava Nidāna), the classic of diagnosis, compiled from the words of many sages.

name: Śārṅgadhara (author of the medical Saṃhitā)
summary: Author of the Śārṅgadhara Saṃhitā, a handbook of pharmacy with the classic account of pulse examination.
notes: Identity with the anthologist of the Śārṅgadharapaddhati (tch:sarngadhara-anthologist) is debated.

name: Bhāvamiśra
summary: Author of the Bhāvaprakāśa, son of Laṭakana Miśra (colophons).

name: Cakrapāṇidatta
summary: Bengali physician, author of the Āyurvedadīpikā on Caraka, the Bhānumatī on Suśruta and the Cikitsāsaṅgraha (Cakradatta).

name: Ḍalhaṇa
summary: Author of the Nibandhasaṅgraha on the Suśruta Saṃhitā.

name: Gayadāsa
summary: Commentator on the Suśruta Saṃhitā (Nyāyacandrikā), used by Ḍalhaṇa.

name: Aruṇadatta
summary: Author of the Sarvāṅgasundarā on the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya.

name: Hemādri
summary: Lineage contribution (Āyurveda): author of the Āyurvedarasāyana commentary on the Aṣṭāṅgahṛdaya.
notes: Identified by scholars with the Yādava minister and author of the Caturvargacintāmaṇi.

name: Jejjaṭa
summary: Early commentator on the Caraka Saṃhitā (Nirantarapadavyākhyā), partly extant.

name: Bhaṭṭāra Haricandra
summary: Early commentator on the Caraka Saṃhitā (Carakanyāsa), known from fragments.

name: Indu (commentator on the Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha)
summary: Author of the Śaśilekhā commentary on the Aṣṭāṅgasaṅgraha; in some accounts a pupil of Vāgbhaṭa.
notes: Pupil relation recalled only.

name: Vijayarakṣita
summary: Began the Madhukośa commentary on the Mādhava Nidāna.

name: Śrīkaṇṭhadatta
summary: Pupil of Vijayarakṣita who completed the Madhukośa.

name: Śivadāsa Sena
summary: Bengali commentator; author of the Carakatattvapradīpikā.

name: Gaṅgādhara Kaviratna
summary: Bengali physician and scholar who edited and commented on the Caraka Saṃhitā (Jalpakalpataru).

name: Āḍhamalla
summary: Commentator on the Śārṅgadhara Saṃhitā (Dīpikā).

name: Kāśīrāma Vaidya
summary: Commentator on the Śārṅgadhara Saṃhitā (Gūḍhārthadīpikā).

name: Vṛnda
summary: Author of the Siddhayoga (Vṛndamādhava).

name: Tīsaṭa
summary: Author of the Cikitsākalikā.

name: Vaṅgasena
summary: Author of a large Cikitsāsārasaṅgraha.

name: Soḍhala
summary: Author of the Gadanigraha.

name: Govinda Dāsa
summary: Author to whom the Bhaiṣajyaratnāvalī is attributed.
notes: Date uncertain.

name: Lolimbarāja
summary: Poet-physician, author of the Vaidyajīvana.

name: Mādhava Upādhyāya
summary: Author of the Āyurvedaprakāśa on mercurial and mineral medicine.

name: Narahari Paṇḍita
summary: Author of the Rāja Nighaṇṭu.

name: Madanapāla
summary: King under whose name the Madanapāla Nighaṇṭu was composed.

name: Kaiyadeva
summary: Author of the Kaiyadeva Nighaṇṭu.

name: Nīlamegha
summary: Author of the Tantrayuktivicāra.

name: Ravigupta
summary: Author of the Siddhasāra.

name: Ugrāditya
summary: Jain author of the Kalyāṇakāraka, an Āyurveda without meat, alcohol or honey.

name: Pālakāpya
summary: The sage of elephant medicine (Hastyāyurveda).

name: Jayadatta Sūri
summary: Author of the Aśvavaidyaka.

name: Surapāla
summary: Author of the Vṛkṣāyurveda.

name: Śiva (as Bhairava, the revealer of rasa)
summary: Lineage contribution (Rasa Śāstra): as Bhairava he answers the Goddess in the Rasārṇava; mercury is 'equal to me, born from my limbs, the rasa of my body' (Rasārṇava 1.36).

name: Pārvatī (the Goddess, questioner of the Rasārṇava)
summary: Lineage contribution (Rasa Śāstra): the Goddess who asks Bhairava about the jīvanmukti hinted at in all the tantras but never disclosed (Rasārṇava 1.6).

name: Govinda (author of the Rasahṛdayatantra)
summary: Author of the Rasahṛdayatantra; the Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha calls him Govinda Bhagavatpāda and lists him among the siddhas who attained jīvanmukti in a mercurial body (Raseśvara 12); counted among the twenty-seven siddhas (Rasaratnasamuccaya 1.4).
notes: Tradition (SDS) calls him Govinda Bhagavatpāda; whether he is Śaṅkara's teacher (tch:govinda-bhagavatpada) is denied by scholars. Kept separate.

name: Nityanātha
summary: Lineage contribution (Rasa Śāstra): author of the five-part Rasaratnākara, who says he gathered only what he learnt from his guru's mouth and experienced himself (Rasa-khaṇḍa 1.22) and named his work with the claim 'what is elsewhere is here; what is here is nowhere else' (1.25).

name: Carpaṭanātha
summary: Lineage contribution (Rasa Śāstra): cited as a rasa authority in the Rasaratnākara (Rasa-khaṇḍa 1.17: 'what the siddha Carpaṭi taught') and listed as 'Carvaṭi' among those liberated in life by a mercurial body (SDS Raseśvara 12).

name: Vyāḍi (the rasa-siddha)
summary: Counted among the twenty-seven siddhas of rasa (Rasaratnasamuccaya 1.3) and, as 'Vyāli', among those liberated in life (SDS Raseśvara 12).
notes: Relation to the grammarian Vyāḍi (tch:vyadi) not established; kept separate.

name: Sarvajña Rāmeśvara Bhaṭṭāraka
summary: Named in the Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha (Raseśvara 22) with Govinda Bhagavatpāda as an ancient teacher who expounded the processings of mercury.

name: Somadeva (author of the Rasendracūḍāmaṇi)
summary: Author of the Rasendracūḍāmaṇi.

name: Yaśodhara (rasa author)
summary: Author of the Rasaprakāśasudhākara.

name: Śālinātha
summary: Author of the Rasamañjarī.

name: Ḍhuṇḍhukanātha
summary: Author to whom a Rasendracintāmaṇi is attributed.

name: Gopālakṛṣṇa (rasa author)
summary: Author to whom the Rasendrasārasaṅgraha is attributed.

name: Manthānabhairava
summary: Named among the rasa authorities in the Rasaratnasamuccaya (1.6); the Ānandakanda is attributed to him in some accounts.

name: Kaṅkālayogin
summary: Author to whom the Rasādhyāya is attributed.

name: Merutuṅga (commentator on the Rasādhyāya)
summary: Jain author of a commentary on the Rasādhyāya.

name: Cāmuṇḍa (rasa author)
summary: Author to whom the Rasasaṃketakalikā is attributed.

name: Cūḍāmaṇi Miśra
summary: Author to whom the Rasakāmadhenu is attributed.

name: Sadānanda Śarmā
summary: Author of the Rasataraṅgiṇī, a modern textbook of rasa medicine.

name: Kākacaṇḍīśvara
summary: Named among the authorities of rasa (Rasaratnasamuccaya 1.6); the Kākacaṇḍīśvarīmata bears his name.
